title.zh: 卷248 列傳三十五 许定国 左梦庚 田雄 张天禄 孙可望
title.en: Volume 248 Biographies 35: Xu Dingguo, Zuo Menggeng, Tian Xiong, Zhang Tianlu, Sun Kewang
title.raw: 卷248 列傳三十五 许定国 左梦庚 田雄 张天禄 孙可望

sentences.zh: 列傳三十五

translations.literal: Biographies 35
translations.idiomatic: Biography 35

sentences.zh: =許定國=許定國，河南太康人。

translations.literal: Xu Dingguo. Xu Dingguo was a native of Taikang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dingguo, a native of Taikang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎間，官山西總兵官。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign of Ming, he served as regional commander of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era of the Ming dynasty, he held the post of Shanxi regional commander.

sentences.zh: 李自成圍開封，趣定國赴援，師次沁水，一夕師潰，逮治論死。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng; [the court] urged Dingguo to reinforce; his army halted at Qinshui; in one night the army collapsed; he was arrested and judged deserving death.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng, Dingguo was ordered to the rescue. His force halted at Qinshui, but overnight the army disintegrated. He was arrested and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 尋复授援剿河南總兵官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed regional commander for relieving and suppressing Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed regional commander charged with relieving and pacifying Henan.

sentences.zh: 福王時，駐軍睢州。

translations.literal: During the Prince of Fu, he garrisoned troops at Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, he garrisoned his troops at Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，豫親王多鐸下河南，次孟津，定國使請降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Prince Yu Dodo advanced into Henan, halted at Mengjin; Dingguo sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, Prince Yu Dodo marched into Henan and encamped at Mengjin. Dingguo dispatched envoys offering submission.

sentences.zh: 肅親王豪格略山東，复上書請以其孥來附，肅親王命遣子為質。

translations.literal: Prince Su Haoge pacified Shandong; [Dingguo] again wrote requesting to bring his family to attach; Prince Su ordered sending his son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Su Haoge was pacifying Shandong, Dingguo wrote again asking to bring his family over. Prince Su ordered him to send his son as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣其子詣肅親王軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, he sent his son to Prince Su's army.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he sent his son to Prince Su's camp.

sentences.zh: 明督師大學士史可法遣總兵高傑徇河南，次歸德，聞定國已遣子納款，招往會，不赴。

translations.literal: Ming supervising secretary Grand Secretary Shi Kefa dispatched regional commander Gao Jie to campaign in Henan, halted at Guide; hearing Dingguo had already sent his son to submit, [Shi] summoned [Dingguo] to join, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming supervising secretary Grand Secretary Shi Kefa sent regional commander Gao Jie to operate in Henan. Jie halted at Guide, heard that Dingguo had already sent his son to surrender to the Qing, and summoned him to a meeting, but Dingguo refused to come.

sentences.zh: 傑乃與巡撫越其傑、巡按陳潛夫就定國睢州，定國不得已郊迎。

translations.literal: Jie then with provincial governor Yue Qijie and surveillance commissioner Chen Qianfu went to Dingguo's Suizhou; Dingguo had no choice but to greet them in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then went with Provincial Governor Yue Qijie and Surveillance Commissioner Chen Qianfu to Dingguo's base at Suizhou, and Dingguo had no choice but to meet them outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 其傑勸傑勿入城，傑輕定國，不聽。

translations.literal: Qijie urged Jie not to enter the city; Jie looked down on Dingguo and did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Qijie urged Jie not to enter the city, but Jie despised Dingguo and would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 既入，定國宴傑，侑以妓。

translations.literal: Once inside, Dingguo feasted Jie, assisted by courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: After they entered, Dingguo entertained Jie at a banquet with singing girls in attendance.

sentences.zh: 傑酣，為定國刻行期，並微及遣子納款事。

translations.literal: Jie became drunk; he set a departure date for Dingguo and subtly touched on the matter of sending his son to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jie drank heavily, pressed Dingguo for a date to march, and obliquely brought up his son's surrender to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 定國益懼，中夜伏兵殺傑。

translations.literal: Dingguo grew still more afraid; at midnight he set ambush troops and killed Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo grew more frightened still and, in the middle of the night, had hidden troops kill Jie.

sentences.zh: 明日，傑部將攻定國屠城。

translations.literal: The next day, Jie's subordinate generals attacked Dingguo and slaughtered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jie's officers attacked Dingguo and put the city to the sword.

sentences.zh: 定國走考城，遂來降。

translations.literal: Dingguo fled to Kaocheng, then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo fled to Kaocheng and then submitted to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 豫親王請以定國從征，留其孥曹縣，命河道總督楊方興厚贍之。

translations.literal: Prince Yu requested that Dingguo follow on campaign; his family was left at Caoxian; he ordered Grand Canal director-general Yang Fangxing to support them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu asked that Dingguo accompany the campaign, left his family at Caoxian, and ordered Grand Canal Director-General Yang Fangxing to provide for them generously.

sentences.zh: 定國妻邢有疾，乞還鄉里，方興為代奏。

translations.literal: Dingguo's wife Xing was ill; she begged to return to her home district; Fangxing memorialized on her behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo's wife, the Xing clan, fell ill and asked to return home; Fangxing submitted a memorial on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 命暫居曹縣，俟定國入覲。

translations.literal: He was ordered to reside temporarily at Caoxian, awaiting Dingguo's audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: She was ordered to remain at Caoxian until Dingguo came to the capital for an audience.

sentences.zh: 豫親王師還，定國詣京師，隸漢軍鑲白旗。

translations.literal: Prince Yu's army returned; Dingguo went to the capital and was enrolled in the Bordered White Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu's army withdrew, Dingguo went to the capital and was enrolled in the Han Eight Banners' Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he died.

sentences.zh: 五年，以來降功，授一等精奇尼哈番，子爾安襲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for the merit of coming to surrender, he was granted first-class jingqi niha; his son Er'an inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5, for the merit of his submission, he was granted a first-class jingqi niha rank, which his son Er'an inherited.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔求言，爾安為睿親王多爾袞訟功德，請修其墓。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict sought opinions; Er'an pleaded the merits and virtues of Prince Rui Dorgon and requested repair of his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12, when the throne called for memorials, Er'an spoke up for Prince Rui Dorgon's achievements and asked that his tomb be restored.

sentences.zh: 語詳睿親王傳。

translations.literal: The account is detailed in the biography of Prince Rui.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biography of Prince Rui.

sentences.zh: 坐煽惑，減死流寧古塔。

translations.literal: Convicted of incitement, his death sentence was reduced and he was exiled to Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of sedition, he was spared execution and banished to Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 弟爾吉襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Erji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Erji inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 史可法置江北四鎮，傑與劉澤清、劉良佐、黃得功分領之。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa established the four garrisons north of the Yangtze; Jie with Liu Zeqing, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong each commanded one.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa set up the four garrisons north of the Yangtze, which Jie, Liu Zeqing, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong commanded in turn.

sentences.zh: 傑為定國所殺，得功戰死蕪湖。

translations.literal: Jie was killed by Dingguo; Degong died in battle at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was killed by Dingguo, and Degong fell in battle at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 劉良佐，直隸人，明總兵，預擁立福王。

translations.literal: Liu Liangzuo, a native of Zhili, Ming regional commander, took part beforehand in enthroning the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liangzuo, a Zhili native who had been a Ming regional commander, helped install the Prince of Fu on the throne.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，豫親王下江南，良佐以兵十萬來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Prince Yu descended on Jiangnan; Liangzuo came to surrender with an army of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2, as Prince Yu advanced into Jiangnan, Liangzuo surrendered with a force of one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 江南定，詣京師，隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he went to the capital and was enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified, he went to the capital and was enrolled in the Han Eight Banners' Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 五年，以來降功，授世職二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for the merit of coming to surrender, he was granted hereditary second-class jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5, for the merit of his submission, he received a hereditary second-class jingqi niha rank.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍譚泰討金聲桓。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Tan Tai in suppressing Jin Shengheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Tan Tai in the campaign against Jin Shengheng.

sentences.zh: 師還，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was made a minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授江南江安提督，加總管銜。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was appointed Jiangnan Jiang'an provincial commander, with the added title of zongguan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 he was appointed provincial commander of Jiang'an in Jiangnan, with the added rank of zongguan.

sentences.zh: 尋改直隸提督，改左都督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Zhili provincial commander and made Left Censor-in-chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Zhili provincial commander and promoted to Left Censor-in-chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi, on grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he died.

sentences.zh: 劉澤清既降复叛，誅死。

translations.literal: Liu Zeqing, having surrendered, rebelled again and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zeqing, who had surrendered and then rebelled again, was put to death.

sentences.zh: =左夢庚=左夢庚，山東臨清人。

translations.literal: Zuo Menggeng. Zuo Menggeng was a native of Linqing in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Menggeng, a native of Linqing in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父良玉，明史有傳。

translations.literal: His father Liangyu has a biography in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuo Liangyu has a biography in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 良玉初授平賊將軍，及封寧南伯，以平賊將軍印授夢庚。

translations.literal: Liangyu was first appointed Pacification General; when enfeoffed as Baron of Ningnan, he gave the Pacification General seal to Menggeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu was first made Pacification General, and when he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningnan he passed the Pacification General's seal to Menggeng.

sentences.zh: 福王時，良玉舉兵自武昌東下，號「清君側」。

translations.literal: During the Prince of Fu, Liangyu raised troops from Wuchang eastward, proclaiming "Clear the ruler's side."
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Liangyu marched east from Wuchang at the head of an army under the slogan "Clear the ruler's side."

sentences.zh: 次九江，病卒。

translations.literal: He halted at Jiujiang and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Jiujiang and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 諸將推夢庚為帥。

translations.literal: The generals pushed Menggeng to be commander.
translations.idiomatic: The generals chose Menggeng as their commander.

sentences.zh: 總督袁繼咸禦戰，夢庚還駐池州，遣兵間道自彭澤下建德，遂取安慶。

translations.literal: Governor-general Yuan Jixian resisted in battle; Menggeng returned to garrison Chizhou, sent troops by a bypath from Pengze down to Jiande, and then took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yuan Jixian met him in battle. Menggeng withdrew to Chizhou, sent troops by a hidden route from Pengze down toward Jiande, and seized Anqing.

sentences.zh: 總兵黃得功破之銅陵，乃退保九江。

translations.literal: Regional commander Huang Degong defeated him at Tongling; he then withdrew to hold Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Huang Degong defeated him at Tongling, and he fell back to defend Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，英親王阿濟格逐李自成至九江，夢庚率眾降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Prince Ying Ajige pursued Li Zicheng to Jiujiang; Menggeng led the masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2, Prince Ying Ajige pursued Li Zicheng as far as Jiujiang, and Menggeng surrendered with his army.

sentences.zh: 師還，入覲，宴午門內，命隸漢軍正黃旗。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he had an audience; was feasted inside the Meridian Gate; was ordered enrolled in the Plain Yellow Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was received in audience and entertained inside the Meridian Gate, and was enrolled in the Han Eight Banners' Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「部將盧光祖、李國英從入京師，餘若張應祥、徐恩盛、郝效忠、金聲桓、常登、徐勇、吳學禮、張應元、徐育賢俱奉英親王調發防剿江西、湖廣。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Subordinate generals Lu Guangzu and Li Guoying followed into the capital; the rest, such as Zhang Yingxiang, Xu Ensheng, Hao Xiaozhong, Jin Shengheng, Chang Deng, Xu Yong, Wu Xueli, Zhang Yingyuan, and Xu Yuxian, were all dispatched by Prince Ying to defend and suppress in Jiangxi and Huguang."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "My subordinate generals Lu Guangzu and Li Guoying accompanied me to the capital; the others—Zhang Yingxiang, Xu Ensheng, Hao Xiaozhong, Jin Shengheng, Chang Deng, Xu Yong, Wu Xueli, Zhang Yingyuan, and Xu Yuxian—have all been assigned by Prince Ying to garrison and pacify Jiangxi and Huguang."

sentences.zh: 誠恐諸將在外，踪跡未定，室家未安，訛惑之事，不可不籌。

translations.literal: I truly fear that with the generals abroad, their whereabouts unsettled and their households insecure, matters of rumor and confusion cannot go unplanned for.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that while these officers are away, with their movements uncertain and their families unsettled, rumors and unrest may arise unless provision is made.

sentences.zh: 」命有司安插。

translations.literal: " He was ordered that the responsible offices settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the relevant offices to settle their families.

sentences.zh: 五年，敘來降功，授一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, his merit in coming to surrender was recorded; he was granted first-class jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 his submission was rewarded with a first-class jingqi niha rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，從英親王討大同叛將薑瓖，攻左衛，克之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he followed Prince Ying in suppressing the Datong rebel general Jiang Xiang, attacked Zuowei, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he followed Prince Ying against the Datong rebel Jiang Xiang, attacked Zuowei, and took it.

sentences.zh: 擢本旗固山額真。

translations.literal: He was promoted to gushan ejen of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gushan ejen of his banner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，諡莊敏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he died; posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he died and was given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封一等子。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, his enfeoffment was fixed as first-class viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign his line was fixed at first-class viscount.

sentences.zh: 夢庚諸將，李國英最顯，自有傳。

translations.literal: Among Menggeng's generals, Li Guoying was most illustrious and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Of Menggeng's officers, Li Guoying rose highest and has a biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 郝效忠，遼東人，隸漢軍正白旗。

translations.literal: Hao Xiaozhong, a native of Liaodong, enrolled in the Plain White Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xiaozhong, a Liaodong native, served in the Han Eight Banners' Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 從英親王定湖南，擢湖南右路總兵，加都督僉事，授世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Ying in pacifying Hunan, was promoted to Hunan Right Route regional commander, given Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military, and granted hereditary third-class ada haha.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Ying in pacifying Hunan, was made Hunan Right Route regional commander with the rank of Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military, and received a hereditary third-class ada haha rank.

sentences.zh: 孫可望陷沅州，效忠率師克黎平。

translations.literal: Sun Kewang captured Yuanzhou; Xiaozhong led troops and recovered Liping.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Kewang took Yuanzhou, Xiaozhong led a force and recaptured Liping.

sentences.zh: 可望兵驟至，力戰，馬蹶被執，不屈，遂見殺，贈都督同知。

translations.literal: Kewang's troops arrived suddenly; he fought fiercely; his horse stumbled and he was captured; he would not submit and was then killed; posthumously granted Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang's army arrived in force. Xiaozhong fought hard until his horse fell and he was taken. He refused to yield and was killed, and was posthumously made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 徐勇，亦遼東人。

translations.literal: Xu Yong was also a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yong was also from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 英親王檄署九江總兵，調黃州，捕治九江、黃州土寇。

translations.literal: Prince Ying by dispatch appointed him acting Jiujiang regional commander, transferred him to Huangzhou, and had him capture and punish local bandits in Jiujiang and Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying appointed him acting regional commander of Jiujiang, then transferred him to Huangzhou to suppress local bandits in both prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明唐王使招之，勇斬使以聞，命移鎮長沙。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Tang sent envoys to recruit him; Yong beheaded the envoys and reported it; he was ordered to transfer his garrison to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Tang sent envoys to win him over; Yong executed them and reported the matter, and was ordered to move his command to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛，招勇，复斬其使。

translations.literal: Jin Shengheng rebelled and recruited Yong; he again beheaded the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shengheng rebelled and tried to recruit him, Yong again executed the envoys.

sentences.zh: 與李錦戰江中，中矢，裹創戰愈奮。

translations.literal: He fought Li Jin on the river; was struck by an arrow; bound his wound and fought still more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Li Jin on the river, was hit by an arrow, bound his wound, and fought on with greater fury.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城，設策守禦，錦遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked the city; he devised plans to defend; Jin fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels besieged the city he organized the defense, and Li Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 迎鄭親王師擊破明大學士何騰蛟。

translations.literal: He welcomed Prince Zheng's army and together defeated Ming Grand Secretary He Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Prince Zheng's army and together they defeated the Ming Grand Secretary He Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 復調辰常總兵，授世職一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: He was again transferred as Chen-Chang regional commander and granted hereditary first-class ada haha together with toosara ha.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as regional commander of Chen and Chang, and granted a hereditary first-class ada haha rank together with toosara ha.

sentences.zh: 明桂王遣將張光翠、張景春窺辰州，屯荔溪。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui sent generals Zhang Guangcui and Zhang Jingchun to spy on Chenzhou and encamped at Lixi.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui sent Zhang Guangcui and Zhang Jingchun to probe Chenzhou and encamped at Lixi.

sentences.zh: 勇督將士渡江戰，擊殺景春，擒裨將六，馘士卒數百，加左都督，進世職三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: Yong directed officers and soldiers to cross the river and fight; he killed Jingchun, captured six lieutenant generals, took several hundred enemy heads, was given Left Censor-in-chief of the Military, and advanced to hereditary third-class ashana niha.
translations.idiomatic: Yong led his men across the river, killed Jingchun, captured six subordinate commanders, and took several hundred heads. He was made Left Censor-in-chief of the Military and advanced to a hereditary third-class ashana niha rank.

sentences.zh: 桂王復遣白文選來攻，驅象為陣，破城，勇巷戰死之，贈太子太保，進世職二等，諡忠節。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui again sent Bai Wenxuan to attack; he drove elephants as battle array; the city was breached; Yong died fighting in the lanes; posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; advanced to hereditary second class; posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui sent Bai Wenxuan again with war elephants in the van. The city fell, and Yong died fighting in the streets. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, advanced to a hereditary second-class rank, and given the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 以其兄子襲，入籍武昌衛。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son inherited; enrolled in the Wuchang guard.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son inherited the rank and was enrolled in the Wuchang guard.

sentences.zh: 盧光祖，遼東海州人，隸漢軍鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: Lu Guangzu, a native of Haizhou in Liaodong, enrolled in the Bordered Blue Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangzu, from Haizhou in Liaodong, served in the Han Eight Banners' Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 從肅親王下四川，破張獻忠。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Su into Sichuan and defeated Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Su into Sichuan and defeated Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 授夔州總兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed Kuizhou regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regional commander of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 擊破明桂王將硃天麟等。

translations.literal: He defeated the Ming Prince of Gui's generals Zhu Tianlin and others.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Ming Prince of Gui's generals Zhu Tianlin and others.

sentences.zh: 取順慶，屢捕治土寇。

translations.literal: He took Shunqing and repeatedly captured and punished local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He took Shunqing and repeatedly suppressed local bandits.

sentences.zh: 甘一爵、硃德洪據鄰水、大竹為亂。

translations.literal: Gan Yijue and Zhu Dehong held Linshui and Dazhu in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Yijue and Zhu Dehong seized Linshui and Dazhu and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 光祖督師討之，戰七晝夜，斬一爵、德洪，降硐寨十餘。

translations.literal: Guangzu directed troops to suppress them; fought seven days and nights; beheaded Yijue and Dehong; more than ten stockade forts surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu led the campaign against them, fought for seven days and nights, killed Yijue and Dehong, and received the surrender of more than ten stockade forts.

sentences.zh: 以功授世職一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted hereditary first-class ada haha.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he received a hereditary first-class ada haha rank.

sentences.zh: 孫可望破敘州，將軍李國翰率師赴援，光祖殿，遇敵，戰敗，命立功自贖。

translations.literal: Sun Kewang broke Xuzhou; General Li Guohan led troops to relieve; Guangzu brought up the rear, met the enemy, was defeated, and was ordered to redeem himself by merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Kewang took Xuzhou, General Li Guohan marched to relieve the city. Guangzu commanded the rear guard, met the enemy, and was defeated; he was ordered to redeem himself through further service.

sentences.zh: 尋改川北總兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made North Sichuan regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regional commander of northern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓既降复叛，誅死。

translations.literal: Jin Shengheng, having surrendered, rebelled again and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shengheng, who had surrendered and then rebelled again, was put to death.

sentences.zh: =田雄=田雄，直隸宣化人。

translations.literal: Tian Xiong. Tian Xiong was a native of Xuanhua in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xiong, a native of Xuanhua in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 馬得功，遼東人。

translations.literal: Ma Degong, a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Degong, a Liaodong native.

sentences.zh: 仕明皆至總兵。

translations.literal: Serving Ming, both rose to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming both had risen to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，豫親王多鐸下江南，明福王由崧走蕪湖。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Prince Yu Dodo descended on Jiangnan; the Ming Prince of Fu Zhu Yousong fled to Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2, as Prince Yu Dodo advanced into Jiangnan, the Ming Prince of Fu Zhu Yousong fled toward Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 巴牙喇纛章京圖賴督兵截江斷道，雄、得功縛福王及其妃來獻，豫親王令以原銜從征。

translations.literal: Bayalara dazan janggin Tulai directed troops to cut the river and block the road; Xiong and Degong bound the Prince of Fu and his consort and came to present them; Prince Yu ordered them to follow the campaign with their original titles.
translations.idiomatic: Bayalara dazan janggin Tulai blocked the river crossings. Xiong and Degong captured the Prince of Fu and his consort and brought them in. Prince Yu allowed them to follow the campaign under their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 尋授雄杭州總兵，得功鎮江總兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Xiong was appointed Hangzhou regional commander and Degong Zhenjiang regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was soon made regional commander of Hangzhou and Degong of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 雄佐總督張存仁、梅勒章京珠瑪喇，駐軍杭州。

translations.literal: Xiong assisted Governor-general Zhang Cunren and meile janggin Zhumala, garrisoning troops at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong served under Governor-General Zhang Cunren and meile janggin Zhumala, with his army garrisoned at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時明魯王以海稱「監國」紹興，乘間渡錢塘江窺杭州，雄與存仁、珠瑪喇等屢擊破之。

translations.literal: At the time the Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai styled himself "Overseer of the State" at Shaoxing; seizing an opportunity he crossed the Qiantang River to spy on Hangzhou; Xiong with Cunren, Zhumala, and others repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai had styled himself regent at Shaoxing and, seizing an opening, crossed the Qiantang to threaten Hangzhou. Xiong, Zhang Cunren, Zhumala, and others repeatedly drove him back.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Zhejiang provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he was promoted to Zhejiang provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，發李成棟逆書，加左都督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he uncovered Li Chengdong's treasonous letter and was given Left Censor-in-chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he exposed Li Chengdong's treasonous correspondence and was made Left Censor-in-chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 八年，敘來降功，授世職一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, his merit in coming to surrender was recorded; he was granted hereditary first-class jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 his submission was rewarded with a hereditary first-class jingqi niha rank.

sentences.zh: 明魯王與其臣阮進、張名振等據舟山，雄與固山額真金礪以舟師出海擒進，遂破舟山，隳其城，名振擁魯王入海。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Lu with his ministers Ruan Jin, Zhang Mingzhen, and others held Zhoushan; Xiong with gushan ejen Jin Kan took a fleet to sea and captured Jin, then broke Zhoushan and destroyed its walls; Mingzhen escorted the Prince of Lu out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu, with Ruan Jin, Zhang Mingzhen, and others, held Zhoushan. Xiong and gushan ejen Jin Kan took a fleet to sea, captured Jin, stormed Zhoushan, and razed its walls. Mingzhen then escorted the Prince of Lu out to sea.

sentences.zh: 十二年，進將阮思、陳六禦等復據舟山，朝命寧海大將軍伊爾德率師南征。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, advancing generals Ruan Si, Chen Liuyu, and others again held Zhoushan; the court ordered Grand General Ninghai Ierde to lead troops south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12, Ruan Si, Chen Liuyu, and other Ming commanders reoccupied Zhoushan, and the court ordered Grand General of the Eastern Seas Ierde to lead a southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 雄預治戰艦攻具，分兵遣裨將扼要隘，通聲援，而以舟師會伊爾德擊思，以橫洋、金塘為舟山要路，分兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Xiong prepared warships and siege equipment in advance, divided troops and sent lieutenant generals to hold strategic passes, maintained communications for mutual support, and with a fleet joined Ierde to attack Si; taking Hengyang and Jintang as the key routes to Zhoushan, he divided troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong prepared warships and siege gear in advance, posted subordinate commanders at key passes, kept lines of communication open, and joined Ierde's fleet against Ruan Si. He identified Hengyang and Jintang as the critical approaches to Zhoushan and sent detachments to break both positions.

sentences.zh: 張兩翼夾擊，殲其眾無算，思赴水死。

translations.literal: Zhang deployed both wings in a pincer attack, annihilated their forces beyond counting; Si drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked from both wings, destroyed the enemy in great numbers, and Ruan Si drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was given Junior Tutor together with Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On news of victory he was made Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，疏請歸旗籍，隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he memorialized requesting return to banner registration and enrollment in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 he asked to return to banner registration and was enrolled in the Han Eight Banners' Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功兵擾浙境，陷遂安、平陽諸縣。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong's troops harassed the Zhejiang border and captured Suian, Pingyang, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong's forces raided the Zhejiang frontier and took Suian, Pingyang, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾雄，上命寬之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War impeached Xiong; the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War impeached Xiong, but the emperor ordered clemency.

sentences.zh: 十六年，成功兵攻太平，擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Chenggong's troops attacked Taiping; [Xiong] repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16, when Chenggong attacked Taiping, Xiong drove him back.

sentences.zh: 復攻寧波，雄督戰，分三路進剿，成功兵引退。

translations.literal: He again attacked Ningbo; Xiong directed the fighting, advanced in three columns to suppress, and Chenggong's troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong attacked Ningbo again. Xiong directed operations in three columns and forced him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 十八年，進二等侯。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was advanced to second-class marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 he was promoted to second-class marquis.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，卒，贈太傅，諡毅勇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, he died; posthumously granted Grand Tutor; posthumous title Yiyong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Yiyong.

sentences.zh: 得功，亦隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Degong was also enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: Degong also served in the Han Eight Banners' Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 江寧初定，明瑞昌王誼泐屯花山、龍潭間。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was first pacified, the Ming Prince of Ruichang Zhu Yile garrisoned between Huashan and Longtan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Jiangning was pacified, the Ming Prince of Ruichang Zhu Yile encamped between Huashan and Longtan.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，謀攻江寧，事泄，走鎮江。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, he plotted to attack Jiangning; the affair leaked; he fled to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he plotted an attack on Jiangning, but the plan was exposed and he fled to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 得功獲誼泐，誅之。

translations.literal: Degong captured Yile and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Degong captured Yile and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 尋以收劫盜入伍，降調。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for enrolling bandits into the ranks, he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted for enrolling bandits into his command.

sentences.zh: 四年，大學士洪承疇請以得功署副將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou requested that Degong be appointed acting vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4, Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou asked that Degong be made acting vice commander.

sentences.zh: 從浙閩總督張存仁剿建寧、邵武山寇，克松溪、政和、建陽、崇安、光澤諸縣，即令駐松溪。

translations.literal: He followed Zhe-Fujian Governor-general Zhang Cunren in suppressing mountain bandits in Jianning and Shaowu, captured Songxi, Zhenghe, Jianyang, Chong'an, Guangze, and other counties, and was immediately ordered to garrison Songxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhe-Fujian Governor-General Zhang Cunren against mountain rebels in Jianning and Shaowu, took Songxi, Zhenghe, Jianyang, Chong'an, Guangze, and other counties, and was ordered to remain at Songxi.

sentences.zh: 复克慶元、永春、德化諸縣。

translations.literal: He again captured Qingyuan, Yongchun, Dehua, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also recovered Qingyuan, Yongchun, Dehua, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 六年，授右路總兵，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Right Route regional commander and given Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he was made Right Route regional commander with the rank of Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 克南安，破海寇林忠。

translations.literal: He captured Nan'an and defeated the sea bandit Lin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He took Nan'an and defeated the pirate Lin Zhong.

sentences.zh: 复捕治興​​化、仙遊、惠安諸縣海寇鄭丹國等。

translations.literal: He again captured and punished the sea bandits Zheng Danguo and others in Xinghua, Xianyou, Hui'an, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also suppressed the pirates Zheng Danguo and others in Xinghua, Xianyou, Hui'an, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功據廈門。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張學聖诇成功方出，令得功攻廈門，克之。

translations.literal: Provincial governor Zhang Xuesheng learned that Chenggong had just gone out and ordered Degong to attack Xiamen; he captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Zhang Xuesheng learned that Chenggong was away and ordered Degong to attack Xiamen, which fell.

sentences.zh: 成功還救，复陷。

translations.literal: Chenggong returned to relieve it and again took it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong returned to the rescue and recaptured the city.

sentences.zh: 遂圍漳州，破海澄。

translations.literal: He then besieged Zhangzhou and broke Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Zhangzhou and stormed Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 得功退守泉州，與固山額真金礪會師解漳州圍。

translations.literal: Degong withdrew to hold Quanzhou and joined forces with gushan ejen Jin Kan to lift the siege of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Degong fell back to Quanzhou and joined gushan ejen Jin Kan to relieve the siege of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以得功初克廈門貪取財物為成功所乘，命逮治，援赦免。

translations.literal: Because when Degong first captured Xiamen he greedily seized goods and Chenggong took advantage of this, he was ordered arrested and tried, but pardoned on appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Because Degong had looted Xiamen when he first took it, giving Chenggong his opening, he was ordered arrested but pardoned on appeal.

sentences.zh: 十一年，敘前功，賜一品頂帶，出鎮泉州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, his earlier merit was recorded; he was given a first-rank official's hat knob and sent out to garrison Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 his earlier service was recognized with a first-rank hat knob, and he was posted to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 得功自陳與雄同降，援雄例乞世職，授一等精奇尼哈番，加都督同知。

translations.literal: Degong stated that he had surrendered together with Xiong, cited Xiong's precedent in requesting a hereditary office, and was granted first-class jingqi niha and made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: Degong noted that he had surrendered with Xiong, cited Xiong's precedent in asking for a hereditary rank, and received a first-class jingqi niha together with the rank of Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢福建提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was promoted to Fujian provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 he was promoted to Fujian provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 林忠复據永春、德化、尤溪、大田諸縣，巡撫宜永貴令得功率師討之。

translations.literal: Lin Zhong again held Yongchun, Dehua, Youxi, Datian, and other counties; Provincial Governor Yi Yonggui ordered Degong to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zhong reoccupied Yongchun, Dehua, Youxi, Datian, and other counties. Provincial Governor Yi Yonggui ordered Degong to lead a campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 師行，寇自閩安迳攻會城，得功引師還，與城兵夾擊，圍解。

translations.literal: As the army marched, bandits from Min'an took a direct route to attack the provincial capital; Degong led the army back and, with the capital troops in a pincer, lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: While his army was on campaign, rebels from Min'an struck straight at the provincial capital. Degong turned back and, with the garrison, drove them off in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與浙閩總督李率泰等合兵克閩安，成功屢內犯，得功擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he joined Zhe-Fujian Governor-general Li Shuaitai and others in combined forces to capture Min'an; Chenggong repeatedly raided inland and Degong repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 14 he joined Zhe-Fujian Governor-General Li Shuaitai and others to take Min'an. Chenggong raided inland repeatedly, and Degong drove him back each time.

sentences.zh: 十八年，進三等侯。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was advanced to third-class marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 he was promoted to third-class marquis.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，遷濱海居民內地，擊敗海寇阻民遷者。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, coastal inhabitants were moved inland; he defeated sea bandits who obstructed the relocation.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1, as coastal populations were moved inland, he defeated pirates who tried to block the relocation.

sentences.zh: 二年，師進攻廈門，得功克烏沙，以舟師出海。

translations.literal: In the second year, the army advanced to attack Xiamen; Degong captured Wusha and took a fleet to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2, as the army advanced on Xiamen, Degong took Wusha and put to sea with his fleet.

sentences.zh: 南風起，寇乘上流來戰，得功奮擊，沒於陣。

translations.literal: A south wind rose; the bandits used the upstream current to come and fight; Degong fought fiercely and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When a south wind rose, the enemy used the current to attack from upstream. Degong fought hard and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 李率泰以聞，進一等侯，諡襄武。

translations.literal: Li Shuaitai reported it; [Degong] was advanced to first-class marquis; posthumous title Xiangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuaitai reported his death. Degong was posthumously promoted to first-class marquis with the title Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 子三奇，襲爵，官至潮州總兵。

translations.literal: His son Sanqi inherited the title and rose to Chaozhou regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sanqi inherited the title and eventually became regional commander of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，定諸侯、伯封號，雄曰順義，得功曰順勤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, the designations for marquises and earls were fixed: Xiong was called Shunyi, Degong Shunqin.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 14 the formal titles for marquises and earls were fixed: Xiong received Shunyi and Degong Shunqin.

sentences.zh: =張天祿=張天祿，陝西榆林人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianlu. Zhang Tianlu was a native of Yulin in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianlu, a native of Yulin in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明季與弟天福以義勇從軍，積功至總兵。

translations.literal: Late in Ming he and his younger brother Tianfu joined the army as volunteers and through accumulated merit rose to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Ming he and his younger brother Tianfu joined the army as volunteers and rose through merit to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 福王時，大學士史可法督師，令屯瓜洲為前鋒。

translations.literal: During the Prince of Fu, Grand Secretary Shi Kefa supervised the army and ordered him to garrison Guazhou as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Grand Secretary Shi Kefa, as supervising secretary, stationed him at Guazhou as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 豫親王師下江南，天祿、天福率所部三千人從趙之龍迎降，豫親王令以原官從征，隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu's army descended on Jiangnan, Tianlu and Tianfu led their three thousand men to follow Zhao Zhilong in welcoming surrender; Prince Yu ordered them to follow the campaign with their original offices and enrolled them in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu's army entered Jiangnan, Tianlu and Tianfu led three thousand men with Zhao Zhilong to submit. Prince Yu let them keep their former ranks on campaign and enrolled them in the Han Eight Banners' Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 明僉都御史金聲家休寧，受唐王命，糾鄉勇十餘萬據徽州。

translations.literal: Ming Vice Censor-in-chief Jin Sheng was from Xiuning; receiving the Prince of Tang's order, he gathered more than one hundred thousand militia and held Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Vice Censor-in-chief Jin Sheng, a native of Xiuning, obeyed the Prince of Tang's order, raised more than one hundred thousand militiamen, and seized Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 貝勒博洛遣固山額真葉臣率師擊之，天祿及總兵卜從善、李仲興、劉澤泳並從。

translations.literal: Beile Bolo dispatched gushan ejen Ye Chen to lead troops against him; Tianlu and regional commanders Bu Congshan, Li Zhongxing, and Liu Zeyong all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Bolo sent gushan ejen Ye Chen against him, with Tianlu and regional commanders Bu Congshan, Li Zhongxing, and Liu Zeyong in support.

sentences.zh: 師自旌德入，戰績溪，獲聲及中軍吳國禎、副將成有功、守備萬全等，送江寧殺之。

translations.literal: The army entered from Jingde, fought at Jixi, captured Sheng and central army commander Wu Guozhen, vice commander Cheng Yougong, garrison commander Wan Quan, and others, and sent them to Jiangning for execution.
translations.idiomatic: The army entered from Jingde and fought at Jixi. Jin Sheng, Central Army Commander Wu Guozhen, Vice Commander Cheng Yougong, Garrison Commander Wan Quan, and others were captured and sent to Jiangning for execution.

sentences.zh: 徽州平。

translations.literal: Huizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 明大學士黃道周率兵犯徽州，天祿擊之，斬其將程嗣聖等十餘人，獲總兵李堯光等。

translations.literal: Ming Grand Secretary Huang Daozhou led troops to invade Huizhou; Tianlu attacked him, beheaded his generals Cheng Sisheng and more than ten others, and captured regional commander Li Yaoguang and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Grand Secretary Huang Daozhou marched on Huizhou. Tianlu met him, killed more than ten of his officers including Cheng Sisheng, and captured Regional Commander Li Yaoguang and others.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，戰婺源，獲道周，亦送江寧殺之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, he fought at Wuyuan, captured Daozhou, and also sent him to Jiangning for execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he fought at Wuyuan, captured Daozhou, and sent him to Jiangning for execution as well.

sentences.zh: 分兵出祁門、江灣、街口、黃源，四道逐捕道周餘眾。

translations.literal: He divided troops out through Qimen, Jiangwan, Jiekou, and Huangyuan, four routes pursuing and capturing Daozhou's remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments out by four routes—Qimen, Jiangwan, Jiekou, and Huangyuan—to hunt down Daozhou's remaining forces.

sentences.zh: 以功加都督同知，授徽寧池太總兵官。

translations.literal: For merit he was given Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military and appointed regional commander of Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Military and appointed regional commander over Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 天祿屯徽州城外，依山為營。

translations.literal: Tianlu garrisoned outside Huizhou city and made camp against the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlu camped outside Huizhou on the hillside.

sentences.zh: 值雨，父老迎天祿入城，天祿曰：「三軍方在泥塗，何忍獨安？

translations.literal: It happened to rain; the elders welcomed Tianlu into the city; Tianlu said: "The whole army is still in the mud—how can I bear to rest alone in comfort?"
translations.idiomatic: During a rainstorm the local elders invited Tianlu into the city. He replied, "The whole army is still standing in the mud—how can I alone seek comfort?"

sentences.zh: 」終不下山。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not come down from the hill.
translations.idiomatic: He never left the hillside camp.

sentences.zh: 軍民皆稱之。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians alike praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 明嵩安王常淇糾眾數千擾婺源，天祿率副將許漢鼎等擊之，獲常淇及監軍江於東等。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Song'an Chang Qi gathered several thousand men to harass Wuyuan; Tianlu led Vice Commander Xu Handing and others to attack them and captured Qi and supervising commander Jiang Yudong and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Song'an Chang Qi raised several thousand men to raid Wuyuan. Tianlu led Vice Commander Xu Handing and others against them and captured Qi, Supervising Commander Jiang Yudong, and their followers.

sentences.zh: 四年，授江南提督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Jiangnan provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 he was appointed Jiangnan provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，敘來降功，授世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, his merit in coming to surrender was recorded; he was granted hereditary third-class ada haha.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 his submission was rewarded with a hereditary third-class ada haha rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，進三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was advanced to third-class jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 he was advanced to third-class jingqi niha.

sentences.zh: 九年，鄭成功圍漳州，命天祿赴援，成功引退。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Zheng Chenggong besieged Zhangzhou; Tianlu was ordered to go to relieve it, and Chenggong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9, when Zheng Chenggong besieged Zhangzhou, Tianlu was sent to relieve the city and Chenggong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天祿留駐延平，捕治山寇。

translations.literal: Tianlu remained garrisoned at Yanping and captured and punished mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlu remained at Yanping to suppress mountain rebels.

sentences.zh: 十一年，明魯王將張名振攻崇明，天祿還松江禦戰。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Ming Prince of Lu's general Zhang Mingzhen attacked Chongming; Tianlu returned to Songjiang to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11, Zhang Mingzhen, a general of the Ming Prince of Lu, attacked Chongming, and Tianlu returned to Songjiang to meet him.

sentences.zh: 名振既出海，复侵吳淞。

translations.literal: After Mingzhen had gone out to sea, he again invaded Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzhen put to sea, he raided Wusong again.

sentences.zh: 我水師與戰，敗績。

translations.literal: Our naval forces fought him and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Our fleet engaged him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 江南總督馬鳴佩劾天祿失舟師三百餘及砲械，匿未報；

translations.literal: Jiangnan Governor-general Ma Mingpei impeached Tianlu for losing more than three hundred vessels and artillery, concealing it and not reporting;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan Governor-General Ma Mingpei impeached Tianlu for losing more than three hundred ships and their guns without reporting it;

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督佟泰劾天祿與名振通書：逮下刑部，讞通書無​​據，坐匿失砲械等，奪官，降世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-general Tong Tai impeached Tianlu for corresponding with Mingzhen; he was arrested and sent to the Ministry of Justice; the verdict found no basis for correspondence, but convicted him of concealing the loss of artillery and the like; his office was stripped and his hereditary rank reduced to third-class ada haha.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Tong Tai accused him of corresponding with Mingzhen. He was sent to the Ministry of Justice; the charge of treasonous correspondence was not sustained, but he was convicted of concealing the naval losses, stripped of office, and reduced to a hereditary third-class ada haha rank.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 he died.

sentences.zh: 天福初降，從征崑山、嘉定。

translations.literal: When Tianfu first surrendered, he followed campaigns at Kunshan and Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianfu first submitted, he took part in the campaigns at Kunshan and Jiading.

sentences.zh: 民不薙發，據城抗我師，天福與總兵李成棟討平之。

translations.literal: The people would not shave their heads; they held the cities and resisted our army; Tianfu with regional commander Li Chengdong suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the people refused the queue edict and held their cities against our forces, Tianfu and Regional Commander Li Chengdong put the resistance down.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，授陝西漢羌總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed Shaanxi Han-Qiang regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 he was appointed regional commander of the Han and Qiang frontier in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 敘來降及戰功，授世職一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: His merit in coming to surrender and battle achievements were recorded; he was granted hereditary first-class ashana niha.
translations.idiomatic: For his submission and battlefield service he received a hereditary first-class ashana niha rank.

sentences.zh: 明山陰王鼎濟聚兵據毛壩關，署單一涵為元帥。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Shanyin Wang Dingji gathered troops and held Maoba Pass, appointing Shan Yihan as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Shanyin Wang Dingji raised troops and seized Maoba Pass, making Shan Yihan his commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 年六，天福自漢中率師入山，獲鼎濟，一涵投崖死。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Tianfu from Hanzhong led troops into the mountains, captured Dingji, and Yihan threw himself off a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6, Tianfu marched from Hanzhong into the hills, captured Dingji, and Yihan leaped from a cliff to his death.

sentences.zh: 參將王永祥叛延安，山寇劉宏才攻同官，天福先後討平之。

translations.literal: Adjutant Wang Yongxiang rebelled at Yan'an; mountain bandit Liu Hongcai attacked Tongguan; Tianfu in succession suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Wang Yongxiang rebelled at Yan'an, and the mountain rebel Liu Hongcai attacked Tongguan; Tianfu suppressed both in turn.

sentences.zh: 以病還京師，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he returned to the capital and was appointed minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital on grounds of illness and was made a minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授本旗都統。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was appointed dutong of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 he was made dutong of his banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he died.

sentences.zh: =趙之龍=趙之龍，江南虹縣人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhilong. Zhao Zhilong was a native of Hong County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhilong, a native of Hong County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，以忻城伯鎮南京。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen, as Baron of Xincheng he garrisoned Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era he held Nanjing as Baron of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 福王立，與擁戴，干政。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he took part in installing him and meddled in government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he helped install him and meddled in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 豫親王師至，與魏國公徐允爵，保國公張國弼，隆平侯張拱日，臨淮侯李祖述，懷寧侯孫維城，靈壁侯湯國祚，安遠侯柳祚昌，永昌侯徐宏爵，定遠侯鄧文囿，項城伯常應俊，大興伯鄒存義，寧晉伯劉允極，南和伯方一元，東寧伯焦夢熊，安城伯張國才，洛中伯黃九鼎，成安伯郭祚永，駙馬齊贊元，大學士王鐸，尚書錢謙益，侍郎硃之臣、梁雲構、李綽等迎降。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu's army arrived, he with Duke of Wei Xu Yunjue, Duke of Bao Zhang Guobi, Marquis of Longping Zhang Gongri, Marquis of Linhuai Li Zushu, Marquis of Huaining Sun Weicheng, Marquis of Lingbi Tang Guozuo, Marquis of Anyuan Liu Zuochang, Marquis of Yongchang Xu Hongjue, Marquis of Dingyuan Deng Wenyou, Baron of Xiangcheng Chang Yingjun, Baron of Daxing Zou Cunyi, Baron of Ningjin Liu Yunji, Baron of Nanhe Fang Yiyuan, Baron of Dongning Jiao Mengxiong, Baron of Ancheng Zhang Guocai, Baron of Luozhong Huang Jiuding, Baron of Cheng'an Guo Zuoyong, imperial son-in-law Qi Zanyuan, Grand Secretary Wang Duo, Minister Qian Qianyi, Vice Ministers Zhu Zhichen, Liang Yungou, Li Chuo, and others welcomed surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu's army arrived, Zhilong joined Duke of Wei Xu Yunjue, Duke of Bao Zhang Guobi, Marquis of Longping Zhang Gongri, Marquis of Linhuai Li Zushu, Marquis of Huaining Sun Weicheng, Marquis of Lingbi Tang Guozuo, Marquis of Anyuan Liu Zuochang, Marquis of Yongchang Xu Hongjue, Marquis of Dingyuan Deng Wenyou, Baron of Xiangcheng Chang Yingjun, Baron of Daxing Zou Cunyi, Baron of Ningjin Liu Yunji, Baron of Nanhe Fang Yiyuan, Baron of Dongning Jiao Mengxiong, Baron of Ancheng Zhang Guocai, Baron of Luozhong Huang Jiuding, Baron of Cheng'an Guo Zuoyong, Imperial Son-in-law Qi Zanyuan, Grand Secretary Wang Duo, Minister Qian Qianyi, Vice Ministers Zhu Zhichen, Liang Yungou, Li Chuo, and others in welcoming the Qing.

sentences.zh: 之龍授世職三等阿思哈尼哈番，允爵等皆置勿用。

translations.literal: Zhilong was granted hereditary third-class ashana niha; Yunjue and the others were all set aside and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong received a hereditary third-class ashana niha rank, while Yunjue and the other nobles were passed over.

sentences.zh: 鐸等詣京師。

translations.literal: Duo and the others went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Duo and the others went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是北都降者多授原官，御史盧傳言南都新人不得與舊臣比。

translations.literal: Earlier, those who surrendered at the Northern Capital were mostly given their original offices; Censor Lu Chuan said that newcomers from the Southern Capital could not be compared with old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, defectors from the northern capital had usually kept their former offices, but Censor Lu Chuan argued that the southern newcomers should not be treated like long-serving Qing officials.

sentences.zh: 鐸至，命以尚書管弘文院學士，累擢至禮部尚書，卒，諡文安。

translations.literal: When Duo arrived, he was ordered as Minister to oversee Hongwen Academy academician; he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites; died; posthumous title Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo arrived he was made Minister with charge of the Hongwen Academy, rose eventually to Minister of Rites, died, and was given the posthumous title Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 謙益語在文苑傳。

translations.literal: Qianyi's account is in the literary biography.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi is treated in the literary biographies.

sentences.zh: =孫可望=孫可望，陝西延長人。

translations.literal: Sun Kewang. Sun Kewang was a native of Yanchang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang, a native of Yanchang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 從張獻忠為賊，與李定國、劉文秀、艾能奇並為獻忠養子。

translations.literal: He followed Zhang Xianzhong as a bandit; with Li Dingguo, Liu Wenxiu, and Ai Nengqi he was alike an adopted son of Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhang Xianzhong as a rebel, and he, Li Dingguo, Liu Wenxiu, and Ai Nengqi were all Xianzhong's adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 獻忠據四川，使分將其眾，可望號平東將軍。

translations.literal: Xianzhong held Sichuan and had them each command part of his forces; Kewang styled himself Pacification General of the East.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhong held Sichuan he divided his forces among them; Kewang took the title Pacification General of the East.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，肅親王豪格師定四川，獻忠敗死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, Prince Su Haoge's army pacified Sichuan; Xianzhong was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3, Prince Su Haoge's army pacified Sichuan and Xianzhong was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 可望與定國等率殘眾南竄，道重慶、綦江、遵義入貴陽。

translations.literal: Kewang with Dingguo and others led the remnant masses south in flight, by way of Chongqing, Qijiang, and Zunyi into Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang, Dingguo, and the others fled south with the remnants of the army, passing through Chongqing, Qijiang, and Zunyi into Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 阿迷土司沙定洲亂雲南，可望率眾兼程赴之。

translations.literal: The Aimi chieftain Sha Dingzhou rebelled in Yunnan; Kewang led his forces day and night to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Aimi chieftain Sha Dingzhou rebelled in Yunnan, Kewang marched day and night to intervene.

sentences.zh: 定洲方攻楚雄，迎戰大敗，走歸阿迷。

translations.literal: Dingzhou was just then attacking Chuxiong; he met them in battle and was greatly defeated, fleeing back to Aimi.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou was besieging Chuxiong when Kewang arrived; he was routed and fled back to Aimi.

sentences.zh: 可望入雲南會城，遣定國徇迤東，而與文秀率兵西出，得副使楊畏知，相誓扶明室，與俱至楚雄，略迤西諸府。

translations.literal: Kewang entered the Yunnan provincial capital, sent Dingguo to campaign in the eastern circuit, while he with Wenxiu led troops west, obtained Vice Commissioner Yang Weizhi, mutually swore to support the Ming house, went with him to Chuxiong, and pacified the prefectures of the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang entered the Yunnan capital, sent Dingguo to secure the eastern circuit, and marched west with Wenxiu. He won over Vice Commissioner Yang Weizhi, swore with him to restore the Ming, advanced to Chuxiong, and brought the western prefectures under control.

sentences.zh: 定國亦定迤東諸府。

translations.literal: Dingguo also pacified the prefectures of the eastern circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo likewise pacified the eastern prefectures.

sentences.zh: 可望遂盡有雲南，自號平東王，以乾支紀年，鑄錢曰「興朝通寶」。

translations.literal: Kewang then wholly possessed Yunnan, styled himself King Who Pacifies the East, dated by the sexagenary cycle, and cast coin reading "Xingchao Tongbao."
translations.idiomatic: Kewang then held all of Yunnan, proclaimed himself King Who Pacifies the East, dated his reign by the sexagenary cycle, and minted coins inscribed "Xingchao Tongbao."

sentences.zh: 時能奇已前死，可望並將其眾。

translations.literal: At the time Nengqi had already died earlier; Kewang also took command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: By then Nengqi had already died, and Kewang absorbed his troops as well.

sentences.zh: 定國、文秀故等夷，不為可望下。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxiu had originally been his equals and would not submit to Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu had once been his equals and would not bow to him.

sentences.zh: 可望假事杖定國，欲以威眾，隙益深。

translations.literal: Kewang on a pretext had Dingguo beaten with the staff, wishing thereby to awe the masses; the rift grew still deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang had Dingguo flogged on a pretext to intimidate the others, and the breach between them widened.

sentences.zh: 明桂王在肇慶，乃遣畏知奉表乞王封，桂王封可望景國公，賜名朝宗。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui was at Zhaoqing; he then sent Weizhi to present a memorial requesting princely enfeoffment; the Prince of Gui enfeoffed Kewang as Duke of Jing and bestowed the name Chaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui was at Zhaoqing and sent Weizhi with a memorial requesting a royal title. The prince enfeoffed Kewang as Duke of Jing and gave him the name Chaozong.

sentences.zh: 使以敕印往，而桂王諸將爭欲得可望為強援。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent with the edict and seal, but the Prince of Gui's generals all contended to gain Kewang as a strong reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent with the patent and seal, but the Prince of Gui's generals all competed to secure Kewang as a powerful ally.

sentences.zh: 堵胤錫駐梧州，承製改封平遼王；

translations.literal: Du Yinxian was garrisoned at Wuzhou and, assuming imperial authority, changed the enfeoffment to King Who Pacifies Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: Du Yinxian, stationed at Wuzhou, assumed imperial authority and changed the title to King Who Pacifies Liaodong;

sentences.zh: 陳邦傅守泗城，又矯命封秦王；

translations.literal: Chen Bangfu held Sicheng and again by forged order enfeoffed him as King of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bangfu, holding Sicheng, forged another order enfeoffing him as King of Qin;

sentences.zh: 可望乃不受景國公命。

translations.literal: Kewang then did not accept the Duke of Jing appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang therefore refused the title of Duke of Jing.

sentences.zh: 會我師克韶州，桂王走梧州。

translations.literal: It happened that our army captured Shaozhou; the Prince of Gui fled to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When our army took Shaozhou, the Prince of Gui fled to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 可望復遣使請封，議封澂江王。

translations.literal: Kewang again sent envoys requesting enfeoffment; it was discussed to enfeoff him as King of Chengjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang sent envoys again to request a title, and the court considered making him King of Chengjiang.

sentences.zh: 使者謂非秦不敢復命，大學士嚴起恆持不可，議中寢。

translations.literal: The envoy said that unless it were Qin he dared not return with a reply; Grand Secretary Yan Qiheng held that it could not be done; the discussion was dropped midway.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said he could not return unless the title were King of Qin. Grand Secretary Yan Qiheng objected, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 可望襲貴陽，復遣文秀攻嘉定，入四川。

translations.literal: Kewang attacked Guiyang, again sent Wenxiu to attack Jiading, and entered Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang seized Guiyang, sent Wenxiu against Jiading, and advanced into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 我師定兩廣，桂王至南寧，乃遣使封可望冀王，可望猶不受，復使畏知詣桂王，而遣其將賀九儀等以五千人先驅，取起恆及諸臣阻秦封者盡殺之。

translations.literal: Our army pacified Liang-Guang; the Prince of Gui reached Nanning; he then sent envoys to enfeoff Kewang as King of Ji; Kewang still did not accept; he again sent Weizhi to the Prince of Gui, while dispatching his generals He Jiuyi and others with five thousand men as vanguard, seized Qiheng and all ministers who had opposed the Qin enfeoffment, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: After our forces pacified Guangdong and Guangxi, the Prince of Gui reached Nanning and offered Kewang the title King of Ji. Kewang still refused. He sent Weizhi to the prince again, but also dispatched He Jiuyi and others with five thousand men ahead of him to seize and kill Qiheng and every minister who had opposed making him King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 桂王乃真封可望秦王，而留畏知授大學士。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui then truly enfeoffed Kewang as King of Qin, while retaining Weizhi and appointing him Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui at last enfeoffed Kewang as King of Qin and kept Weizhi at court as Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 可望聞之怒，召至貴陽面數之，畏知以冠擊可望，亦被殺。

translations.literal: Kewang heard it and was angry; he summoned [Weizhi] to Guiyang and rebuked him to his face; Weizhi struck Kewang with his cap and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang was furious when he heard of it. He summoned Weizhi to Guiyang and rebuked him to his face. Weizhi struck him with his official cap and was killed in turn.

sentences.zh: 桂王遣大學士文安之督師四川，將以招川中諸鎮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui dispatched Grand Secretary Wen Anzhi to supervise the army in Sichuan, intending thereby to win over the various garrisons of the province.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui sent Grand Secretary Wen Anzhi to command in Sichuan, hoping to win over the garrisons there.

sentences.zh: 可望遣兵伺於都勻，邀止之。

translations.literal: Kewang sent troops to watch at Duyun and intercepted and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang posted troops at Duyun to intercept and stop him.

sentences.zh: 可望將移桂王自近，挾以作威。

translations.literal: Kewang was about to move the Prince of Gui nearer to himself and use him to display power.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang planned to bring the Prince of Gui closer so he could rule through him.

sentences.zh: 桂王奔廣南，可望遣兵迎入安隆所，改為安龍府，歲供銀八千、米百石，窮迫不可堪；

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui fled to Guangnan; Kewang sent troops to welcome him into Anlong subprefecture, changed it to Anlong prefecture, supplied eight thousand taels of silver and one hundred shi of grain yearly; the distress was unbearable;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui fled to Guangnan. Kewang brought him into Anlong, elevated it to a prefecture, and allowed him only eight thousand taels of silver and one hundred shi of grain a year—misery he could scarcely endure;

sentences.zh: 而馬吉祥、龐天壽輩方欲戴可望行禪讓，可望遂自設內閣六部等官，立太廟，定朝儀，改印文為八疊。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Ma Jixiang, Pang Tianshou, and their sort were just then wishing to install Kewang in an abdication; Kewang then on his own established Grand Secretariat, Six Ministries, and other offices, erected the Imperial Ancestral Temple, fixed court ritual, and changed document seals to eight folds.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Ma Jixiang, Pang Tianshou, and others were urging Kewang to take the throne by abdication. He set up his own Grand Secretariat and Six Ministries, founded an ancestral temple, fixed court ritual, and changed official seals to an eight-fold style.

sentences.zh: 桂王益憂懼。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui grew still more anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui grew more fearful still.

sentences.zh: 初，定國自廣西入湖廣，兵益強，不復禀可望約束。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dingguo from Guangxi entered Huguang; his troops grew stronger; he no longer reported to or obeyed Kewang's constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dingguo had marched from Guangxi into Huguang, his army growing stronger until he no longer obeyed Kewang.

sentences.zh: 會定國敗於衡州，使召詣沅州議事，將以為罪而殺之；

translations.literal: It happened that Dingguo was defeated at Hengzhou; [Kewang] sent to summon him to Yuanzhou to discuss affairs, intending to convict him of a crime and kill him;
translations.idiomatic: When Dingguo was defeated at Hengzhou, Kewang summoned him to Yuanzhou on the pretext of consultation, intending to kill him for the defeat;

sentences.zh: 定國辭不赴，又自柳州攻肇慶，下高、廉、雷諸府。

translations.literal: Dingguo declined and did not go; he again from Liuzhou attacked Zhaoqing and took the prefectures of Gao, Lian, and Lei.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo refused to come. From Liuzhou he attacked Zhaoqing and overran the prefectures of Gao, Lian, and Lei.

sentences.zh: 至是，桂王聞定國兵強，密詔使入衛。

translations.literal: By this time the Prince of Gui heard that Dingguo's troops were strong and secretly ordered envoys to come and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Prince of Gui heard how strong Dingguo's army had become and secretly summoned him to his protection.

sentences.zh: 可望聞，使執大學士吳貞毓等，凡預謀者盡殺之。

translations.literal: Kewang heard it and had Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and others arrested; all who had taken part in the plot were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang learned of it, he arrested Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and others and killed everyone involved in the plot.

sentences.zh: 議移桂王貴陽，使其將白文選督行期。

translations.literal: It was discussed to move the Prince of Gui to Guiyang; he had his general Bai Wenxuan supervise the schedule of the move.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to move the Prince of Gui to Guiyang and put Bai Wenxuan in charge of the transfer.

sentences.zh: 文選心不直可望，以情輸桂王，緩其行。

translations.literal: Wenxuan's heart was not loyal to Kewang; he confided the situation to the Prince of Gui and slowed the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was disloyal to Kewang, confided in the prince, and delayed the move.

sentences.zh: 俟定國至，奉桂王自安南衛走雲南。

translations.literal: They waited until Dingguo arrived, then escorted the Prince of Gui from Annan guard and fled to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingguo arrived, they escorted the prince from Annan guard into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時文秀守雲南，亦怨可望，迎桂王入雲南會城。

translations.literal: At the time Wenxiu held Yunnan and also resented Kewang; he welcomed the Prince of Gui into the Yunnan provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu was then holding Yunnan and, resenting Kewang as well, welcomed the prince into the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 可望舉兵反桂王，以雙禮留守，令文選統諸軍前行。

translations.literal: Kewang raised troops against the Prince of Gui, left Shuangli to hold the rear, and ordered Wenxuan to command all armies forward.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang took up arms against the prince, left Shuangli in the rear, and sent Wenxuan ahead at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 定國、文秀率師御之，次三岔河，夾水而軍。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxiu led troops to resist him, halted at San Cha River, and encamped on opposite banks.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu marched to meet him, halted at San Cha River, and encamped on opposite banks.

sentences.zh: 文選輕騎奔定國。

translations.literal: Wenxuan with light cavalry fled to Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan rode over to Dingguo with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 可望遣其將張勝、馬寶等自尋甸間道襲雲南，而自率勁卒擊定國等。

translations.literal: Kewang dispatched his generals Zhang Sheng, Ma Bao, and others by a bypath from Xundian to raid Yunnan, while he himself led crack troops to attack Dingguo and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang sent Zhang Sheng, Ma Bao, and others by a hidden route from Xundian against Yunnan, while he led his best troops against Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 戰方合，其將馬惟興先奔，遂大潰，定國遣文秀等追之。

translations.literal: As battle was just joined, his general Ma Weixing fled first; thereupon a great rout; Dingguo sent Wenxiu and others in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Battle had scarcely begun when Ma Weixing fled, and Kewang's army collapsed. Dingguo sent Wenxiu and others in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 可望至貴陽，雙禮紿言追兵且至。

translations.literal: Kewang reached Guiyang; Shuangli deceived him, saying pursuing troops were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang reached Guiyang, where Shuangli deceived him by saying pursuers were close behind.

sentences.zh: 可望知事去，將詣經略洪承疇請降，遣使先納款。

translations.literal: Kewang knew the affair was lost; he was about to go to Pacification Commissioner Hong Chengchou to request surrender and sent envoys first to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing all was lost, Kewang prepared to surrender to Pacification Commissioner Hong Chengchou and sent envoys ahead to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 文秀等遣將楊武追之，及於沙子嶺。

translations.literal: Wenxiu and the others sent General Yang Wu in pursuit and caught up at Shaziling.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent Yang Wu in pursuit and caught up with him at Shaziling.

sentences.zh: 承疇援兵至，乃得脫，將妻子詣長沙降，時順治十四年十月也。

translations.literal: Chengchou's relief troops arrived; only then did he escape; he brought wife and children to Changsha to surrender; it was the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou's reinforcements arrived and he escaped. He took his family to Changsha and surrendered in the tenth month of Shunzhi 14.

sentences.zh: 詔封義王，慰諭之。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him as Prince of Yi and comforted and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed him as Prince of Yi and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 尋遣學士麻勒吉等齎敕印冊封。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Academician Meleji and others were sent bearing the edict, seal, and investiture documents.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Academician Meleji and others were sent with the patent, seal, and investiture documents.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詣京師，命簡親王濟度等郊迎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he went to the capital; Prince Jian Jidu and others were ordered to welcome him in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 he went to the capital, and Prince Jian Jidu and others were ordered to welcome him outside the city.

sentences.zh: 入覲，宴中和殿，賜白金萬，官其部將陳杰，劉天瑞等百餘人，命隸漢軍正白旗。

translations.literal: He had an audience; was feasted in the Hall of Central Harmony; was given ten thousand taels of white silver; his subordinate generals Chen Jie, Liu Tianrui, and more than one hundred others were given offices; they were ordered enrolled in the Plain White Banner of the Han military.
translations.idiomatic: He was received in audience and entertained in the Hall of Central Harmony, given ten thousand taels of silver, and more than a hundred of his officers including Chen Jie and Liu Tianrui were given posts and enrolled in the Han Eight Banners' Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 可望請從討雲南自效，下王大臣議，寢其奏。

translations.literal: Kewang requested to follow in suppressing Yunnan to prove his merit; it was sent down to princes and grand ministers for discussion; his memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang asked to join the Yunnan campaign to prove his loyalty. The memorial was referred to the princes and grand ministers and then shelved.

sentences.zh: 十七年，疏辭封爵，复慰諭之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he memorialized declining enfeoffment; he was again comforted and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 he memorialized asking to decline his title, and was again reassured by the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，諡恪順。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died; posthumous title Keshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was given the posthumous title Keshun.

sentences.zh: 子徵淇襲，未幾卒。

translations.literal: His son Zhengqi inherited; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengqi inherited the title but died soon after.

sentences.zh: 徵淳襲，卒，諡順愍。

translations.literal: Zhengchun inherited; died; posthumous title Shunmin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun inherited, died, and received the posthumous title Shunmin.

sentences.zh: 徵灝請襲，御史孟飛熊疏言：「可望，獻忠餘黨，久據滇、黔，負固不服。

translations.literal: Zhenghao requested inheritance; Censor Meng Feixiong memorialized: "Kewang was a remnant partisan of Xianzhong, long held Yunnan and Guizhou, and stubbornly refused submission."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghao petitioned to inherit. Censor Meng Feixiong wrote: "Kewang was a remnant of Xianzhong's band, long held Yunnan and Guizhou, and stubbornly refused to submit."

sentences.zh: 及為定國所敗，窮蹙來歸，濫膺非分。

translations.literal: When defeated by Dingguo he came to surrender in desperate straits and undeservedly received excessive rank.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Dingguo defeated him did he come in desperation, yet he received honors far beyond his deserts.

sentences.zh: 宜即停止，或以次降等。

translations.literal: It is fitting to stop at once, or reduce the rank by one degree.
translations.idiomatic: The succession should be stopped at once, or the rank reduced by one degree.

sentences.zh: 」下部議，降襲慕義公，官至兵部尚書，諡清端。

translations.literal: " It was sent to the ministries for discussion; inheritance was reduced to Duke of Muyi; he rose to Minister of War; posthumous title Qingduan.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries recommended reducing the inheritance to Duke of Muyi. Zhenghao rose to Minister of War and received the posthumous title Qingduan.

sentences.zh: 子降襲一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: His son Jiang inherited first-class ada haha.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang inherited a first-class ada haha rank.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，命停襲。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, an order stopped inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 the line was ordered discontinued.

sentences.zh: 文選，陝西吳堡人，亦從獻忠為賊。

translations.literal: Wenxuan, a native of Wubu in Shaanxi, also followed Xianzhong as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan, from Wubu in Shaanxi, had also followed Xianzhong as a rebel.

sentences.zh: 獻忠敗，從可望入貴州。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong was defeated, he followed Kewang into Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhong's defeat he followed Kewang into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其緩桂王使得入雲南也，桂王封為鞏國公，令還貴陽慰諭可望，可望奪其兵，置軍中。

translations.literal: In his delaying the Prince of Gui so that he could enter Yunnan, the Prince of Gui enfeoffed him as Duke of Gong and ordered him to return to Guiyang to comfort and instruct Kewang; Kewang stripped him of his troops and placed him in the army.
translations.idiomatic: By delaying the prince's move he allowed him to reach Yunnan. The prince made him Duke of Gong and sent him back to Guiyang to reason with Kewang, but Kewang stripped him of his command and kept him in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 及將舉兵，諸將說可望原得文選為大將，可望使將前鋒，遂降定國，可望以是敗。

translations.literal: When he was about to raise troops, the generals urged Kewang that he had originally had Wenxuan as grand commander; Kewang had him lead the vanguard; he then surrendered to Dingguo; Kewang was thereby defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang prepared to march, his officers reminded him that Wenxuan had once been his chief commander. Kewang put him in the van, but Wenxuan defected to Dingguo, and that was how Kewang lost.

sentences.zh: 桂王封文選鞏昌王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui enfeoffed Wenxuan as King of Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui enfeoffed Wenxuan as King of Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，我師下雲南，定國戰屢敗，令文選為殿；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, our army descended on Yunnan; Dingguo was repeatedly defeated in battle and ordered Wenxuan to bring up the rear;
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 our army entered Yunnan. Dingguo suffered repeated defeats and put Wenxuan in command of the rear guard;

sentences.zh: 戰於玉龍關，文選复敗，走木邦。

translations.literal: They fought at Yulong Pass; Wenxuan was again defeated and fled to Mubang.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated again at Yulong Pass and fled to Mubang.

sentences.zh: 桂王入緬甸，居赭硜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui entered Burma and dwelt at Zhe'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui took refuge in Burma at Zhe'an.

sentences.zh: 十七年，文選攻阿瓦，弗克，與定國會師孟艮；

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Wenxuan attacked Ava and did not take it; he joined Dingguo at Menggen;
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 Wenxuan attacked Ava without success and joined Dingguo at Menggen;

sentences.zh: 再攻阿瓦，求出桂王，終不獲，我師益深入。
